headline: Trump backs Huang's return to Nvidia, but the board resists
dek: The president is open to a return; the board is not, per the Guardian and CNBC.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What happened
body: Donald Trump said he would not oppose Jensen Huang's return to lead Nvidia, per the Guardian.
Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating him, a source told CNBC Technology.

points.t: Law firm Wachtell Lipton is investigating conduct.
The board is focused on the investigation.
Colette Kress runs the company for now.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: Analyst Dan Ives sees "no chance" of Huang returning, per the Guardian.
Shares fell 4.1% on Monday, erasing about $160 billion (Guardian).

items.t: Nvidia is selecting a search firm.
The role could be split between two.

caption.hook: Donald Trump said he would back Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, but the company's board resists.
body: Per the Guardian, Trump said ahead of a trip to Asia that he would not oppose the former CEO's return. CNBC Technology cited a source saying Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back and is focused on its investigation into his conduct, run by law firm Wachtell Lipton. TechRadar, citing the Financial Times, reached the same conclusion.

Colette Kress remains interim CEO, and the company is selecting a search firm. TechRadar names Arm's Rene Haas among those approached. Shares fell 4.1% on Monday, per the Guardian, and analyst Dan Ives says he sees no chance of a return.
caption.cta: Should Nvidia's board listen to Trump on its CEO?
